## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.  
Normalize keys on write so callers can retrieve entries written with mixed-case keys.

## Changes

The pull request adds `Cache.set`, raises the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds, and adds tests for reads after writes, the default TTL constant, and expiration.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Normalize keys before storing entries — After `set("Alpha", 1)`, both `get("Alpha")` and `get("alpha")` return `None`. The setter stores the original key, while `get` lowercases it before lookup. — Mixed-case writes cause cache misses and leave entries that lookup-driven expiration cannot remove.

## Suggestions

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Expire entries at their deadline — An entry written at monotonic time `1000.0` with `ttl=1` is still returned at `1001.0`. The setter records `1001.0` as the deadline, but `get` only expires it when `expires < time.monotonic()`. — Callers reading at the deadline receive a value whose configured lifetime has elapsed. — Fix: Use `expires <= time.monotonic()` at `app/cache.py:21` and extend `test_entries_expire`.
- app/cache.py:7 — comments — Identify 300 seconds as the default TTL — An entry written with `Cache(ttl=1)` has a one-second lifetime despite the comment “Entries expire 300 seconds after they are written.” The setter uses `time.monotonic() + self._ttl`. — The comment gives maintainers the wrong lifetime when callers override the default.
